implementation.summary: Journal probe now streams the Source journal line by line (readline, incremental sha256, generator fed to the real _market_snapshots_from_lines) instead of f.read(). Bounds: 6 GiB size, 64 MiB per line, 900 s probe deadline; each fails closed with a distinct reason (journal_too_large, journal_line_too_long, journal_probe_timeout) whose failure record carries size and bound. Capture proof records journal_lines and probe_seconds (additive, optional on validation). Journal-probe docker call timeout raised 300 -> 1000 s in both Docker.call and GuardedDocker.call; wrapper deadline 1200 -> 1800 s. The new reasons and size/bound travel through failure_record / remote_failure_record, which both the driver and the wrapper use for the workflow failure summary; no separate whitelist exists in those two files.

measurements.not_executed: A real 4 GiB journal was NOT built: the shared /tmp had 4.7 GB free and the write hit ENOSPC at 99 percent. The 4 GiB time claim is an extrapolation from the 200 MiB and 1 GiB runs, not a measurement.

validation.result: 630 passed, 2 skipped (final full run, 271 s). An earlier run had one failure, a wrong line-number expectation in my own new test, since fixed.

unchanged_contract: point_schema, checksum, lineage, snapshot_identity, schema and journal_changed reasons and their line numbers are produced by the same codec calls; the bad_line test shows identical output from the previous and the streaming probe.
residual_risk: Hosted probe duration is unmeasured; if hosted throughput is below ~7 MB/s a journal near 6 GiB would hit journal_probe_timeout (distinct reason, fail closed). nonprod-deploy.yml step timeout was not inspected or changed (outside artifact list).
